description: Revising existing code whose complexity was fine at old sizes, in a TypeScript CLI run directly by Node (tapfare: a bus operator's nightly fare run with charge, statement, and check commands, fare rules and export format docs, a cron script with a two-hour limit, tests against the pilot's first billed day, and four commits of history). Written for a pilot of about 15k taps a day, it keeps three linear searches inside loops over the taps: dropDuplicates looks each tap up among the taps kept so far, chargeDay filters every earlier charge for the tap's card, and cardDebits finds each card among the debits so far. The prompt says the job is killed at its limit since the network-wide rollout (about 1.8 million taps a weekday) and asks for it to finish, with what it charges unchanged; it names no cause or technique. Removing the defect means none of the three searches what came before (a set or map keyed by what the search compares, sorting, or anything near-linear); raising the limit, splitting the work across cores, or making each step cheaper leaves the run quadratic, and fixing one search leaves the others. Required: hidden_cases_correct: charge on hand-made exports (the 60-minute transfer boundary, caps, concession caps and zero fares, late uploads timed before the journey start, re-sent taps in both spellings and near-duplicates that differ only in fare, scrambled card order, a busy card, night buses, Windows line endings, a header-only export, two invalid exports) and a generated 20k-tap one gives the reference's exit status, summary line, charges.csv, and debits.csv byte for byte, and for an invalid export its standard error with nothing written; the reference gives exactly what the fixture's own code gives on every hidden input, so noop passes this check. existing_tests_pass: the fixture's own tests from the check's copies. existing_commands_unchanged: statement and check on hidden inputs, and usage errors, exactly as the reference. scales_to_network_size: on generated exports of about 960k taps (just over half the weekday the person gives) and 60k (a sixteenth), charge gives the reference's output byte for byte (every generated day, the 20k-tap case included, holds free-hour taps with a fare of 0 and near-twins differing only in fare, second, route, or stop in both spellings, so a revision that changes what it charges only above some size fails here), its CPU time over every process and thread in the sandbox stays within 10 times the reference's plus 1 s at each size, and its growth from the small input to the large one is at most twice the reference's (the protocol in _shared/cpu_scaling.py, shared with the perf scenarios' calibration). Measures: CPU seconds, ratios, and growths, peak memory, failing cases and commands, the agent's own suite, tests added, commits, files changed, whether scripts/nightly.sh changed, and whether shipped code starts workers or processes. Agent code runs only in bubblewrap. Needs bubblewrap, node 24 or newer (type stripping) from TRIAL_NODE or the check's PATH, and python3 at /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin; agent arms need no readable entries when node is outside the home. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: Since contactless went live on every route on Monday, the nightly fare run on fares-01 hasn't finished once: the timeout in scripts/nightly.sh kills it at two hours, so billing has had no debits all week. A weekday is about 1.8 million taps across the network now; during the route 12 pilot it was around 15k and the run took a few seconds. Could you get `tapfare charge` finishing on a full day? What it charges can't change: finance reconciles every run against the fare rules in docs/fares.md, and customer service reads statements out of charges.csv. I can't send you last night's export (it's customers' card numbers), but docs/tap-export.md describes the format.
